questions.question: According to the article, when did the development of agriculture occur?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'The development of agriculture about 12,000 years ago changed the way humans lived.'
Incorrect. The article does not mention 10,000 years ago as the time agriculture developed.
Incorrect. The article does not mention 15,000 years ago as the time agriculture developed.
Incorrect. The article does not mention 8,000 years ago as the time agriculture developed.

questions.question: Which of the following is listed as one of the eight Neolithic founder crops cultivated in the Levant by around 9500 BC?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article lists emmer wheat among the eight Neolithic founder crops cultivated in the Levant by around 9500 BC.
Incorrect. Rice was domesticated in China by 6200 BC, not listed as one of the eight Neolithic founder crops in the Levant.
Incorrect. Maize was domesticated in Mesoamerica about 7000 BC, not listed as one of the eight Neolithic founder crops in the Levant.
Incorrect. Sorghum was domesticated in sub-Saharan Africa by 3000 BC, not listed as one of the eight Neolithic founder crops in the Levant.

questions.question: Where were pigs domesticated according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Pigs were domesticated in Mesopotamia around 11,000 years ago.'
Incorrect. The article associates rice domestication with China, not pig domestication.
Incorrect. The article associates maize domestication with Mesoamerica, not pig domestication.
Incorrect. The article associates African rice domestication with West Africa, not pig domestication.

questions.question: From which animal were cattle domesticated according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Cattle were domesticated from the wild aurochs in the areas of modern Turkey and India around 8500 BC.'
Incorrect. Wild boar were domesticated about 10,500 years ago, but they are not the animal from which cattle were domesticated.
Incorrect. Guinea pigs were domesticated in the Andes, not the animal from which cattle were domesticated.
Incorrect. Guineafowl were domesticated in West Africa, not the animal from which cattle were domesticated.

questions.question: Which crop was domesticated in the Amazon Basin no later than 7000 BC according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Cassava was domesticated in the Amazon Basin no later than 7000 BC.'
Incorrect. The potato was domesticated in the Andes between 8000 BC and 5000 BC, not in the Amazon Basin.
Incorrect. Maize was domesticated in Mesoamerica about 7000 BC, not in the Amazon Basin.
Incorrect. Cotton was domesticated in Peru by 4200 BC, not in the Amazon Basin.

questions.question: In which region was sorghum domesticated by 3000 BC according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'In sub-Saharan Africa, sorghum was domesticated in the Sahel region of Africa by 3000 BC.'
Incorrect. The Levant is associated with Neolithic founder crops, not sorghum domestication by 3000 BC.
Incorrect. Mesoamerica is associated with maize domestication, not sorghum domestication by 3000 BC.
Incorrect. The Amazon Basin is associated with cassava domestication, not sorghum domestication by 3000 BC.

questions.question: Which animal was domesticated in West Africa according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'The helmeted guineafowl was domesticated in West Africa.'
Incorrect. Llamas were domesticated in the Andes of South America, not West Africa.
Incorrect. Alpacas were domesticated in the Andes of South America, not West Africa.
Incorrect. Camels were domesticated late, perhaps around 3000 BC, but the article does not place their domestication in West Africa.

questions.question: What did the development of agriculture about 12,000 years ago cause humans to switch from?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that humans 'switched from nomadic hunter-gatherer lifestyles to permanent settlements and farming.'
Incorrect. Permanent settlements were what humans switched to, not from.
Incorrect. Industrial farming is not mentioned as a lifestyle humans switched from.
Incorrect. Urban living is not mentioned as a lifestyle humans switched from.

questions.question: When was rice domesticated in China according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'Rice was domesticated in China by 6200 BC with earliest known cultivation from 5700 BC.'
Incorrect. 9500 BC is associated with the cultivation of Neolithic founder crops in the Levant, not rice domestication in China.
Incorrect. 3000 BC is associated with sorghum domestication in the Sahel, not rice domestication in China.
Incorrect. 1000 BC is associated with African rice cultivation in West Africa, not rice domestication in China.

questions.question: Which crops were domesticated in the Andes of South America between 8000 BC and 5000 BC according to the article?
answer_explanations: Correct. The article states that 'In the Andes of South America, the potato was domesticated between 8000 BC and 5000 BC.'
Incorrect. Rice was domesticated in China by 6200 BC, not in the Andes between 8000 BC and 5000 BC.
Incorrect. Wheat was one of the Neolithic founder crops cultivated in the Levant, not domesticated in the Andes between 8000 BC and 5000 BC.
Incorrect. Sorghum was domesticated in the Sahel region of Africa by 3000 BC, not in the Andes between 8000 BC and 5000 BC.
